subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to Telegram blocked-media diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable root expansion, or should this issue define the canonical host-local media root policy?
rationale: Accepting more host-local paths changes a filesystem/media security boundary, while diagnostics-only work is a smaller UX fix; automation should not choose that permanent contract.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots in the canonical policy item
options.body: Keep this issue focused on clear blocked-media feedback and let the open configurable-root policy item or approved filesystem-roots design own persistent root expansion.

options.title: Define root policy here
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical place to specify and implement a supported configurable media-root contract for Telegram replies.

options.title: Close as documented behavior
options.body: Treat out-of-policy local `MEDIA:` paths as working as designed and require users to stage files into managed roots or use an approved file-read policy path.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots in the canonical policy item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on clear blocked-media feedback and let the open configurable-root policy item or approved filesystem-roots design own persistent root expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest focused history on outbound media access and root-policy plumbing.
